# 0006. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver, not a leaf patcher

**Status:** Accepted, feature-gating superseded by 0007 **Date:** 2026-09-26

**Note (2026-11-02):** `ExtractionOutput` has had a `schemaVersion` since ADR 0017, so the last Consequences bullet no longer applies to it. "Stays free of I/O" means no compiler process: `crates/core` reads and writes files itself (discovery, module resolution, the caches) and spawns nothing.

## Context

The structural resolver can't substitute generics through alias chains or evaluate conditional and mapped types. Ten components account for 2,696 of the 2,720 props missing against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) in the 2026-07-25 baseline (`docs/benchmarks.md`). ADR 0004 deferred a fix until TypeScript 7 offered a usable route.

TypeScript 7.0 has no programmatic API. 7.1 adds one, available now as `tsc --api` in `typescript@next`. RDT's own algorithm runs on it and returned exactly RDT's props on 13 components (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`).

## Decision

Add an opt-in semantic resolver that runs RDT's algorithm on `tsc --api` and merges its result into the structural one per component. Structural stays the default and the fallback.

- `crates/core` defines an owned-data semantic result and does the merge. It stays free of I/O.
- A feature-gated crate spawns `tsc --api`, speaks its protocol and owns the process. Rust spawns it, in the CLI and the NAPI addon alike. The JS client is not involved.
- We pin an exact `typescript` build and check its version at startup, because the protocol has no version handshake.

## Consequences

- Components the structural resolver can't finish get RDT's prop set without a new heuristic per gap.
- The API is `typescript/unstable/*` and still changing. Pinning limits the damage, but a 7.1 change can force rework.
- The backend costs a process per run, so it is off by default.
- Users need `typescript` 7.1 or later. Without it, extraction still succeeds and emits a diagnostic.
- tsc sees a dependency edit only when told, so `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types don't fit `PropType` losslessly, and `ExtractionOutput` has no schema version. A follow-up ADR decides the representation.

# 0007. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default

**Status:** Accepted, discovery not yet implemented **Date:** 2026-10-21

**Note (2026-11-02):** The first Decision bullet (discovery) is not built. `merge_semantic` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`) skips a checker component that has no structural match, and `ComponentEntry` records no origin. The only provenance is the `SemanticBackend` `Info` diagnostic and its `affects` keys. The rest shipped: a runtime opt-in, always compiled in, structural as default and fallback, and `schemaVersion` (ADR 0017).

## Context

ADR 0006 made the TypeScript backend a second resolver that finishes components the structural resolver already found. Detection by shape now covers 92 to 99% of the components react-docgen-typescript (RDT) reports on five large libraries (`docs/edge-cases.md`), and what is left is a call with no type argument (`lazy()`, `createIconLoader("x")`) or a prop a callee adds (Mantine's `component` and `renderRoot` on 220 components). Only the checker can answer those: it knows what the call returns. Separately, callisto's rule is no cargo features in shipped crates, which ADR 0006's "feature-gated crate" contradicts.

## Decision

- **Discovery.** The backend may add components the structural pass did not find, using RDT's rule: a declaration whose type has a call signature with a props-shaped first parameter. Each carries the rule that found it and merges into the structural output; on a clash the structural entry wins.
- **Always compiled, enabled at runtime.** `crates/tsc-client` is a normal dependency of the CLI and the NAPI addon, with no cargo feature. A runtime option turns it on and is off by default, so a run without it spawns nothing.
- **Structural stays the default and the fallback.** A missing, unsupported or crashing `tsc` leaves the structural result untouched and adds a diagnostic.
- **Trigger.** The backend runs only for components the structural pass marked incomplete (an opaque leaf, a wrapper call with no resolved props, a callee-added prop it cannot see) plus whole-project discovery when the option asks for it. It is never a silent default.
- **Output.** `ExtractionOutput` gains an additive `schemaVersion` so consumers can tell whether discovery was on. Existing fields keep their shape.

## Consequences

- Wrapper calls the structural pass cannot see become exact without a new heuristic per library.
- Every build pays for the client's dependencies. Users who never enable the backend pay nothing at runtime.
- The checker needs `typescript` 7.1 or later and sees a dependency edit only when told. `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types do not fit `PropType` losslessly, so a checker answer is converted at the boundary and anything that does not fit stays opaque with a reason.
- Determinism needs a gate: a clean run and an incremental run must agree, measured on the five corpora with dependencies installed.
- Supersedes only the feature-gating bullet of ADR 0006. The rest of 0006 stands.

## Alternatives considered

# 0006. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver, not a leaf patcher

**Status:** Accepted, feature-gating superseded by 0007 **Date:** 2026-09-26

**Note (2026-11-02):** `ExtractionOutput` has had a `schemaVersion` since ADR 0017, so the last Consequences bullet no longer applies to it. "Stays free of I/O" means no compiler process: `crates/core` reads and writes files itself (discovery, module resolution, the caches) and spawns nothing.

## Context

The structural resolver can't substitute generics through alias chains or evaluate conditional and mapped types. Ten components account for 2,696 of the 2,720 props missing against react-docgen-typescript (RDT) in the 2026-07-25 baseline (`docs/benchmarks.md`). ADR 0004 deferred a fix until TypeScript 7 offered a usable route.

TypeScript 7.0 has no programmatic API. 7.1 adds one, available now as `tsc --api` in `typescript@next`. RDT's own algorithm runs on it and returned exactly RDT's props on 13 components (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`).

## Decision

Add an opt-in semantic resolver that runs RDT's algorithm on `tsc --api` and merges its result into the structural one per component. Structural stays the default and the fallback.

- `crates/core` defines an owned-data semantic result and does the merge. It stays free of I/O.
- A feature-gated crate spawns `tsc --api`, speaks its protocol and owns the process. Rust spawns it, in the CLI and the NAPI addon alike. The JS client is not involved.
- We pin an exact `typescript` build and check its version at startup, because the protocol has no version handshake.

## Consequences

- Components the structural resolver can't finish get RDT's prop set without a new heuristic per gap.
- The API is `typescript/unstable/*` and still changing. Pinning limits the damage, but a 7.1 change can force rework.
- The backend costs a process per run, so it is off by default.
- Users need `typescript` 7.1 or later. Without it, extraction still succeeds and emits a diagnostic.
- tsc sees a dependency edit only when told, so `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types don't fit `PropType` losslessly, and `ExtractionOutput` has no schema version. A follow-up ADR decides the representation.

## Alternatives considered

- **Replace `Opaque` leaves with tsc answers** (ADR 0004's model). `OpaqueDetail` holds only a raw string and a reason, and can't be built or inspected outside `crates/core`. Some types resolve to `Named` on purpose with no diagnostic (bare generic parameters, TypeScript utility types), so no leaf marks them.
- **Call the JS client through NAPI.** The CLI is a standalone binary that uses Node only to load `docgen.config.ts`, the binding never calls into JS, and the resolver is synchronous rayon code.
- **Node sidecar**, as `config.rs` does for `docgen.config.ts`. It adds a process hop and a Node dependency. It is the fallback if protocol churn outpaces a Rust client.
- **Vendor typescript-go internals**, as tsgolint does. The repo was closed on 2026-08-20 and the API is the supported surface.
- **TypeScript 7 LSP.** Not evaluated further, because the API exposes each query the algorithm needs directly.

# 0007. Let the backend discover components, always compile it in, and keep structural as the default

**Status:** Accepted, discovery not yet implemented **Date:** 2026-10-21

**Note (2026-11-02):** The first Decision bullet (discovery) is not built. `merge_semantic` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`) skips a checker component that has no structural match, and `ComponentEntry` records no origin. The only provenance is the `SemanticBackend` `Info` diagnostic and its `affects` keys. The rest shipped: a runtime opt-in, always compiled in, structural as default and fallback, and `schemaVersion` (ADR 0017).

## Context

ADR 0006 made the TypeScript backend a second resolver that finishes components the structural resolver already found. Detection by shape now covers 92 to 99% of the components react-docgen-typescript (RDT) reports on five large libraries (`docs/edge-cases.md`), and what is left is a call with no type argument (`lazy()`, `createIconLoader("x")`) or a prop a callee adds (Mantine's `component` and `renderRoot` on 220 components). Only the checker can answer those: it knows what the call returns. Separately, callisto's rule is no cargo features in shipped crates, which ADR 0006's "feature-gated crate" contradicts.

## Decision

- **Discovery.** The backend may add components the structural pass did not find, using RDT's rule: a declaration whose type has a call signature with a props-shaped first parameter. Each carries the rule that found it and merges into the structural output; on a clash the structural entry wins.
- **Always compiled, enabled at runtime.** `crates/tsc-client` is a normal dependency of the CLI and the NAPI addon, with no cargo feature. A runtime option turns it on and is off by default, so a run without it spawns nothing.
- **Structural stays the default and the fallback.** A missing, unsupported or crashing `tsc` leaves the structural result untouched and adds a diagnostic.
- **Trigger.** The backend runs only for components the structural pass marked incomplete (an opaque leaf, a wrapper call with no resolved props, a callee-added prop it cannot see) plus whole-project discovery when the option asks for it. It is never a silent default.
- **Output.** `ExtractionOutput` gains an additive `schemaVersion` so consumers can tell whether discovery was on. Existing fields keep their shape.

## Consequences

- Wrapper calls the structural pass cannot see become exact without a new heuristic per library.
- Every build pays for the client's dependencies. Users who never enable the backend pay nothing at runtime.
- The checker needs `typescript` 7.1 or later and sees a dependency edit only when told. `WatchSession::update_file` must notify it, with a parity test against `extract()`.
- Checker types do not fit `PropType` losslessly, so a checker answer is converted at the boundary and anything that does not fit stays opaque with a reason.
- Determinism needs a gate: a clean run and an incremental run must agree, measured on the five corpora with dependencies installed.
- Supersedes only the feature-gating bullet of ADR 0006. The rest of 0006 stands.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the backend a feature of a separate crate.** Matches ADR 0006 as written but breaks the no-features rule and makes the shipped binary vary by build.
- **Run it by default.** Costs a process per run on projects that structural detection already handles and makes output depend on a toolchain being installed.
- **Add one structural heuristic per remaining shape.** The remaining shapes need the callee's return type; a heuristic per library is what the shape-based detector was built to avoid.

- **What the notes say:** The bullet "`update_file` must notify tsc" is met by dropping answers, not by notifying tsc.

  - **Tests:** Three tests pin it in `crates/core/tests/semantic_hook.rs`.
  - **Not built:** Per-component invalidation (it clears all answers today) and a parity test of a session against `extract()` after an edit.
